from.place: its statement, last sentence: 'An *algebraic closure* $\bar k$ of $k$ is an algebraically closed extension of $k$ which is algebraic over $k$' (the notation $\bar k$ used by the citers presupposes existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism over $k$)

title: Existence and uniqueness of algebraic closures
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. (1) There is an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]: an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ together with a field homomorphism $\iota:k\to\Omega$ such that every element of $\Omega$ is algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-element]. (2) If $(\Omega_1,\iota_1)$ and $(\Omega_2,\iota_2)$ are two algebraic closures of $k$, there is a field isomorphism $\sigma:\Omega_1\to\Omega_2$ with $\sigma\circ\iota_1=\iota_2$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 09GT (fields-theorem-existence-algebraic-closure) for (1); Lemma Tag 09GV (fields-lemma-algebraic-closures-isomorphic) for (2), whose proof produces a morphism of $k$-extensions $\varphi:M\to\overline F$ and shows it is an isomorphism
